messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager - kvcache_continuous_batch_error rate crossed threshold in prod-eu (alerts.kv_cache.errors > 5%)

incident-bot: Links: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1819129876  | Runbook: /runbooks/kvcache-batch

sarah-nguyen: I'm on call, grabbing context. seeing 5xxs + huge latency tail on function-calls route. toolcall paths show batch break loops.

alisha-ops: confirmed - autoscale didnt help, CPU on infer-rtg nodes is fine, but KV cache miss rate jumped from 2%->65% in last 6m. looks like cache key churn.

dmitri-ml: initial theory: structured outputs from recent funcall schema change are preventing prefix reuse, causing batching to break and KV cache fragmentation.

mike-chen: customers complaining about slow chat responses + timeouts. I see retries stacking and queue length up on router.

sarah-nguyen: can someone grep for the recent PR? dmitri, which deploy/commit introduced the schema change?

dmitri-ml: PR #2421 merged 2h ago, commit e7b3f9a. It adds structured output metadata and function args in the first token chunk. This shifts KV cache keys.

alisha-ops: ok plan: 1) disable structured-toolcall variant routing 2) force small batch hotfix (batch_max_tokens=64) 3) evict stale KV entries on affected pools 4) rollback PR if quick revert available.

mike-chen: +1. I'll open emergency hotfix branch. pushing a config-only deploy first so we don't touch model code.

deploy-bot: Deploy started by mike-chen: hotfix/kvcache-batch-20260315 (config-only) -> rolling to prod-eu (3 nodes)

mike-chen: command I ran:
```
redwoodctl deploy --env prod-eu --image redwood/runtime:stable --set batching.max_tokens=64 --set routing.toolcall_structured=false
```

alisha-ops: also triggering KV eviction on pool infer-rtg-2:
```
redwoodctl cache evict --pool infer-rtg-2 --prefix toolcall_v2 --confirm
```

dmitri-ml: while that deploy goes, adding a short-lived traffic rule to route toolcalls to smaller batches and force compatibility:
```
api.routes.update("/v1/toolcall", {batching: {max_tokens: 64, max_batch_size: 1}, fallback_model: "redwood/safe-v1"})
```

sarah-nguyen: FYI, I'm paging SEs for customers with open incidents. impact: ~12 customers, 5 with request timeouts, overall 4xx/5xx spike ~18% above baseline.

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Deploy to prod-eu completed in 90s.

mike-chen: Observability - cache miss rate dropping from 65% -> 18% in 4m. latency p50 improved, p95 still elevated but falling.

alisha-ops: I see throughput returned to normal and queue length draining. No more retries piling.

dmitri-ml: Reproduced locally: structured output fields changed the prompt prefix hashing. We'll add a compatibility layer to normalize function-output metadata before KV key computation. I'll open a follow-up PR.

sarah-nguyen: Great. For now keep the config in place for 4 hours to ensure stability, then gradually relax batching.

mike-chen: Noted. I'm preparing a rollback PR in case anything else regresses, but holding off.

incident-bot: Incident severity updated: SEV3 -> monitoring.

alisha-ops: Customer comms: sent initial note to affected accounts, writing a follow-up summary.

dmitri-ml: Postmortem actions: (1) add unit test for KV key stability on structured outputs (2) add canary for toolcall schema changes (3) make batching change hot-path reversible via feature flag (4) add dashboard for KV churn per-route. I'll own #1 and #2.

sarah-nguyen: I'll own coordination and timeline. mike, please add the config diff + deploy logs to the incident doc. alisha, capture customer impact numbers + notify CSMs.

mike-chen: added logs: deploy id deploy-2026-03-15-4512, commit e7b3f9a-hotfix-01.

alisha-ops: final status at 12:30 UTC: all service checks green, miss rate ~3%, latency back to baseline. leaving the hotfix config in for 3 more hours before reverting.

incident-bot: Incident closed as recovered by sarah-nguyen. Postmortem scheduled for 2026-03-17 16:00 UTC.

sarah-nguyen: thanks team. quick debrief in #eng-runtime after lunch. :thumbsup:
